title: a Result collection returned across a function boundary is discharged by reading an element back out and unwrapping it
notes: specification/failures.mdx:190: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' The second over-correction guard for 07-must-consume/a-returned-result-collection-charges-its-caller, and it is not a duplicate of the Result.all one: `pack()[0]!` never binds the container at all, so it exercises the index-read discharge on an UNBOUND returned collection, where the Result.all case exercises a recognized collector on a bound argument. It is the cross-function spelling of 07-must-consume/an-array-literal-of-results-is-consumed-through-an-index-read, whose refusing twin (`.length` instead of `[0]!`) is 07-must-consume/array-length-is-not-consumption-of-a-result-collection. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-28 by running both backends with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ON, which is when this case first had anything to say: it passed before only because the mandatory option was off. With the option on and the provenance walk unchanged, the reference refused it SMITHERS1207 'postfix ! requires a Result operand' — the specification's own example, refused by the option the specification mandates. The expectation is UNCHANGED at `output`; what changed is that it is now earned. The walk sees through the `| undefined` the ACCESS gained (the container's element type never gained one), and the lowering asserts it in the emitted TypeScript, without which the generated program failed the emit check at TS2345/TS18048. Both backends measured green.
